title: Atomic kernel selector + prefill/decode interleaving causing stale KV refs and precision drift
creator: Aisha Chen
description: Intermittent correctness failures observed in production and stress tests after enabling the new atomic kernel selector and fused-attention kernels. Failures manifest as: (1) small but statistically significant token-level numerical drift leading to unexpected next-token probabilities, and (2) rare decode-time corruption where the model emits repeated token sequences consistent with a stale/overwritten KV pointer. Both failure modes began after the rollout of kernel auto-selection + mixed-precision fused-attn in runtime-1.21.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use runtime-1.21 with kernel_autoselect=true and fused_attn_fp16=true. 2) Run long prefill sessions (~4096 tokens) followed by many interleaved short decode sessions from separate request contexts (simulate 400 concurrent clients). 3) Enable continuous batching and prefix KV caching. 4) Reproduce with model: redwood-open-7b-qlora, sequence length 2048->4096. Observed within 1-10k requests in stress harness. Deterministic repro added in tests/prefill_decode_fuzz with seed 8712.
logs_snippet:
[2026-03-03T14:22:47Z] WARN kernel_selector: selected fused_attn.fp16 for model redwood-open-7b-qlora, runtime_id=rt-22a
[2026-03-03T14:22:47Z] DEBUG prefill: kv_alloc slab=17 ptr=0x7f8b2c4f0 len=4096 owner=request-9f3
[2026-03-03T14:22:47Z] ERROR decode: detected stale-kv-checksum mismatch expected=0x9a2b got=0x7d1c (ctx=request-2be)
[2026-03-03T14:22:47Z] INFO guardrail: falling back to fp32_attn kernel for ctx=request-2be
root_cause: Two interacting regressions: 1) The atomic kernel selector does a lockless map swap of kernel handlers when a new kernel is registered. Under heavy interleaved prefill/decode scheduling, a window exists where a decode thread observes a kernel handle but the KV cache allocator has been rebalanced and reused (slab/TTL) leading to dangling KV pointers. 2) The fused-attn FP16 kernel uses an accumulation path that relies on a slightly different numerical ordering vs. the reference fp32 kernel; in sequences where micro-reordering of token chunks happens (because of batching + prefix cache elimination), we see reproducible but small fp16 rounding drift that changes next-token probabilities enough to trigger downstream behavioral tests.
mitigation: Short-term: (a) disable kernel_autoselect by default for existing clusters (feature-flag rollback), (b) enforce a write memory fence after kernel handle swap, (c) pin critical models to kernel=fallback_fp32 in Dedicated until fix rolls out. Medium-term: add TTL grace window before slab reuse and bump kv-refcount when kernel handler is swapped. Immediate workaround deployed to prod on 2026-03-04 rolled back kernel auto-selection for ~30% of traffic.
proposal: 1) Add atomic versioning to kernel registry: readers must check a monotonic kernel_version and re-read if version changed mid-lookup. 2) Make KV allocator reclaim only after an epoch grace period and add per-request reference counting on KV slabs. 3) Add a correctness-focused test suite: deterministic prefill->interleave fuzz harness, cross-kernel token-level diff tests, and a CI gate running the harness with fused_attn enabled. 4) Roll out kernel-selection changes behind kill-switch and ramp with circuit-breaker metrics (stale-kv-checksum rate). 5) Longer-term: formalize kernel ABI and add a compatibility checker to reject kernel that change accumulation ordering without explicit flag.
